The Maclaurin series for $\ln \left(\frac{1}{1-x}\right)$ is $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{x^{n}}{n}$ with interval of convergence $-1 \leq x<1$.\\
(a) Find the Maclaurin series for $\ln \left(\frac{1}{1+3 x}\right)$ and determine the interval of convergence.\\
(b) Find the value of $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n}}{n}$.\\
(c) Give a value of $p$ such that $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n}}{n^{p}}$ converges, but $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{2 p}}$ diverges. Give reasons why your value of $p$ is correct.\\
(d) Give a value of $p$ such that $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{p}}$ diverges, but $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{2 p}}$ converges. Give reasons why your value of $p$ is correct.
